nodes.description: Public address state variable 'core' holding the privileged owner/minter address; single-step ownership without renounce or two-step transfer.
Public function setCore(address _core) guarded by onlyCore; overwrites the privileged 'core' address in a single step, enabling irreversible transfer of all minting power.
Public function mint(address account, uint256 amount) guarded by onlyCore; invokes internal _mint to create tokens, unbounded inflation surface if core key is compromised.
External function burnForSelf(uint256 amount); burns the caller's own balance via internal _burn with no allowance check.
Constructor initializing ERC20Detailed metadata and assigning core = msg.sender, making the deployer the initial privileged minter.
Modifier onlyCore: require(msg.sender == core, 'Not Authorized') — the sole access-control gate for privileged functions.
Caller-controlled address used in the constructor (core initialization), in the onlyCore authorization check, and as the target of burnForSelf.
State write core = msg.sender in the constructor; privileged owner is set directly from untrusted caller input.
State write core = _core inside setCore; single-step transfer of privileged ownership without two-step confirmation or event-based validation of the new address.
Internal call _mint(account, amount) increasing _totalSupply and _balances; token supply mutation.
Internal call _burn(msg.sender, amount) decreasing caller balance and _totalSupply; state change on caller input.
Parameter _core of setCore; user-supplied new privileged address.
Parameter account of mint; destination address for newly minted tokens.
Parameter amount of mint; quantity of tokens to create.
Parameter amount of burnForSelf; quantity of caller tokens to destroy.

edges.reason: msg.sender is assigned directly to the core state variable during construction, establishing the deployer as privileged owner.
msg.sender is compared against the stored core value inside the onlyCore modifier, which is the sole authorization gate.
The core state variable is read by the onlyCore modifier to validate the caller's privileges.
onlyCore guards setCore, restricting privileged ownership transfer to the current core address.
onlyCore guards mint, restricting token creation to the current core address.
setCore executes the state write core = _core, replacing the access-control authority in a single unverified step.
The _core parameter flows into the core state variable write within setCore.
mint invokes the internal _mint routine to create tokens for the given account.
The account parameter flows into _mint as the recipient of newly created tokens.
The amount parameter flows into _mint as the quantity of tokens created.
burnForSelf invokes the internal _burn routine without any allowance or authorization check.
msg.sender is passed to _burn as the account whose balance is reduced, so a caller can only burn their own tokens.
The amount parameter flows into _burn as the quantity of caller tokens destroyed.

normalization_plan.reason: Parameter _core exists only to supply the core state write in setCore; merge it into the unsafe_operation core = _core.
Parameter account exists only to supply the _mint internal call; merge it into the unsafe_operation _mint(account, amount).
Parameter amount of mint exists only to supply the _mint internal call; merge it into the unsafe_operation _mint(account, amount).
Parameter amount of burnForSelf exists only to supply the _burn internal call; merge it into the unsafe_operation _burn(msg.sender, amount).
